symptom: Real Unity 2022.3.62f2 rejects the candidate bootstrap fixed-byte witness as an unapproved bootstrap reflection entrypoint before fresh M07 fixtures/Players/replay are produced.
directIssue: The M07 policy scan records the H1 fixed ordinary-image Assembly.Load(byte[]) acquisition as a bootstrap reflection reference whose argument is the pinned image SHA-256. BootstrapIsolationRule requires a matching bootstrapEntrypoint declaration, and the frozen dependency policy has no matching H1 entry.
mostLikelyRootCause: The separately reviewed FixedAssemblyBytes acquisition contract for H1CountEarlyStartup.LoadOrdinaryWitness is not integrated with the bootstrap reflection approval path used by M07 policy validation. The count-only build path replaces explicit dependency configuration with an empty bootstrap list and therefore did not exercise this M07 validator boundary.
designGap: V00/V01 and the 132-cell count runner establish tooling/compile/count behavior, but no regression runs the global M07 compiled policy after adding the H1 fixed-byte witness.
impact: V05 successor and independent M08 unavailable
recommendedDirection: Primary should define how a FixedAssemblyBytes bootstrap acquisition is represented in the global policy and make the fixed-image contract and BootstrapIsolationRule agree.

Add a regression that runs M07 ValidateCompilerInputs with the H1CountEarlyStartup fixed-byte site and rejects altered method hash, operation index, image hash, provider identity, and undeclared byte-load sites.
Ensure Invoke-M07Build restores its scene/settings mutation in a finally path when ValidateCompilerInputs fails.
Publish a new source anchor and rerun fresh V00-V05.
localAction: No policy, allowlist, provenance, count, runtime, ABI, or protected-pin change was made. The two workflow-created tracked mutations were captured and restored to exact HEAD blobs.
uncertainty: This failure occurs before fresh M07 resource generation and Players, so it does not establish downstream startup, capacity, coverage, or performance behavior.
